prompt:
Extract a SysML v2 model from the document as a list of facts. Each fact has unit_id (the sentence it comes from), type and slots. Give only the slots that have a value, as a list of {slot, value} pairs; for composition give one 'parts' pair per part.

Types and slots:
  attribute(owner,name,value,unit) action(performer,label) state(owner,label) constraint(subject,expression) requirement(subject,text)
  composition(whole,parts) flow(source,target,payload) succession(before,after) transition(from,to,trigger) allocation(action,to)

Name each element by its full name as first introduced in the document.
RULES:
- Resolve every entity-valued slot using all the text you are given. If a sentence refers to an element by an alias, abbreviation, pronoun or shorter description, write the element's full name as first introduced. If a sentence says an element receives or uses an item and the text you are given states which element produces or sends that item, emit a flow from that producer to the receiver. If an element cannot be determined from the text you are given, use null; never guess.
- Never write placeholder words such as "any", "all", "some state" for an unstated element; use null.
- Do not merge differently named things unless the text says they are the same.
- Emit one action for EVERY behavior verb phrase, including passive voice (performer null), capability statements, displays, logs, generates and reports. label = the verbatim verb phrase with its object.
- Emit a requirement for every NORMATIVE statement (shall, must, should, will, is required to, needs to). Purpose, goal or benefit sentences are not requirements.
- Emit a state for every named mode or state; transitions use the state names, with from null when the prior state is not stated.
- Emit a succession only for an EXPLICIT temporal connective between two actions ("then", "after", "once", "before", "when ... is complete", "next", "finally"); before/after are the action labels. Never use succession for cause or data transfer.
- Resolve a pronoun or "this/these" performer to the element named in the preceding sentence and write that element's name; if it cannot be resolved, use null. Never output a pronoun as a slot value.
- Drop determiners and quantifiers from element names ("Each Soil Moisture Probe" -> "Soil Moisture Probe", "the system" -> "system").
- allocation.to must be a component or actor, never a mode or state.
- Emit a constraint for every threshold, limit, period or deadline stated with a number; expression = the verbatim phrase.
- Emit a flow for every sentence in which an element sends, transmits, reports, displays, commands or delivers an item (target null if the receiver is not named).
 Also list under "entities" every system element, actor or item named in the document units, with its full name and any alias the text explicitly declares for it (e.g. 'hereafter X', 'known as X', 'called X'); aliases [] if none. Return JSON {"entities": [...], "facts": [...]}.

Memory from EARLIER parts of the document (do not extract facts from it; use it only to resolve names, aliases and who produces an item):
Regional Dispatch Center (Juniper): intake/authorized dispatch; preserve uncertainty/rationale; reconcile Caller Location Correction Slip; verify Battery Swap Voucher readiness; use North Approach Queue Snapshot; produce Unit Staging Change Card; update after confirmed transfer; declare threshold-triggered surge; maintain emergency-prioritizing degraded-radio procedure/common operating picture. Computer Aided Dispatch Console: current authorized information/surge/constraints; verify currency. Ambulance Coordination Platform: approved destinations/instructions/timestamped statuses; track accepted mutual aid separately. Call Taker Mara (Larkspur): verify/repeat location first; capture incident/source/pediatric age/available weight/caregiver observations; produce correction slip; confirm incident/facility before transmission; verify Bedside Arrival Receipt timeline. Triage Supervisor (Copperfield): prioritize/reassess/document disagreements; validate surge/protocol priorities; send Pediatric Acuity Note; approve/document temporary overrides beforehand; review audit memo before duplicate closure. Pediatric airway/breathing/circulation/mental-status concerns require prompt escalation. Regional Medical Director: policy/delegation/destination/clinical-surge guidance, no dispatch authority. Dispatcher: compare priority/needs/time/capability/readiness/coverage; compare response-time/coverage before moves. Shift Commander (Sundial): approve coverage-reducing/nonstandard exceptions; escalate destination/access issues; respect clinical authority; send Mutual Aid Release Form; confirm post-surge assignment/constraint/staffing handover. Radio Coordinator (Mistral): verify communications/backups/routes; send assignments/hazards/destinations and Coverage Gap Bulletin; retry/escalate missing acknowledgments; direct fallback channels. Regional Radio Network: en-route/mutual-aid requests/acceptances/updates using agreed call signs; announce outage areas/restoration via remaining channels. Paramedic Crew: acknowledge assignments/destinations/fallbacks, repeat critical locations/destinations before moving; protocol/scope care; pediatric reassessment/change reports to facility; report barriers/request consultation. Ambulance Unit 417: staging/status/arrival/handover reports; moves require confirmation; reassignment requires dispatch-confirmed freedom from care/transport obligations. Fleet Maintenance Cell (Bluejay): promptly report restrictions; defects/clearance; voucher authorizes replacement. Hospital Liaison Desk (Kestrel): confirm pediatric capacity/limitations before destination finalization; record responses in regional coordination record; inform dispatch of unresolved constraints; forward acuity note. Emergency Department: capacity/access/status, acknowledge destination changes, resolve identity/document discrepancies before clearance. Riverside

Document units:
S202: If voice contact fails, dispatchers use the approved data channel when available and record the time of each attempted contact.
S203: Computer Aided Dispatch Console displays the latest confirmed unit status alongside the time and source of that confirmation.
S204: Ambulance Coordination Platform preserves queued status updates during brief connection interruptions and flags records that require reconciliation.
S205: Coverage monitoring compares successful radio checks with the planned check interval for each operating area.
S206: North Gate Status Board and South Gate Status Board provide separate views of access conditions that may affect radio reach or ambulance movement.
S207: Radio Coordinator uses the change card to adjust channel assignments and record the effective time of each change.
S208: Shift Commander receives the Coverage Gap Bulletin and decides whether staffing or deployment adjustments are needed.
S209: Data Quality Officer reviews Pebble for conflicting timestamps before interrupted communications are reconciled.
S210: Triage Supervisor identifies calls whose clinical priority requires immediate radio access and communicates that priority to dispatch staff.
S211: Call Taker Mara keeps the caller connected when feasible while dispatch staff attempt to reach the assigned crew through an approved alternate channel.
S212: Ambulance Unit 417 reports its last confirmed position and safe operating status as soon as contact is restored.
S213: Fleet Maintenance Cell reports radio equipment faults through the established maintenance escalation path.
S214: Hospital Liaison Desk uses available telephone channels to confirm whether receiving facilities can accept arrivals during a network disruption.
S215: Emergency Department staff receive concise arrival updates through the approved backup contact method when radio delivery is unavailable.
S216: Regional Medical Director may advise on clinical prioritization when communication limits materially affect response choices.
S217: Paramedic Crew members follow local safety procedures and do not enter an area where dispatch instructions cannot be confirmed if conditions are uncertain.
S218: Shift Commander retains operational authority until a named successor acknowledges the handover or a higher-level incident command arrangement takes effect.
S219: The outgoing shift records active incidents, communication failures, temporary channel assignments, and decisions awaiting review.
S220: The incoming shift verifies open assignments and confirms which communication paths remain available before accepting control.
S221: After service is restored, dispatch staff reconcile delayed status reports against their recorded timestamps and preserve any unresolved discrepancy for review.
S222: The Regional Dispatch Center maintains controlled procedures for reviewing operational records, approving system changes, and documenting corrective actions.
S223: The Data Quality Officer samples incident records for completeness, timestamp consistency, and alignment between dispatch decisions and recorded outcomes.
